paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: Jesus walked into the hardest night of His life on purpose. He told the three, "My soul is consumed with sorrow to the point of death," and then He fell facedown and prayed, "Yet not as I will, but as You will." (Matthew 26:38-39) He didn't pretend it was easy, and He didn't walk away from it. He brought the honest weight to His Father, and He trusted His Father's will.

Then look at what He could have done. He said He could call on His Father and get more than twelve legions of angels at once, and He said why He didn't: the Scriptures say it must happen this way. (Matthew 26:53-54) Nobody took His life from Him that night. Hold onto that, because it means the cross was no accident. It was God's plan, and Jesus walked into it for people like you and me (Mark 10:45).

And here's the part that hits close to home, baker. The disciples slept when He asked them to watch, and then all of them deserted Him and fled. (Matthew 26:40, 56) Jesus told them, "the spirit is willing, but the body is weak." (Matthew 26:41) I think that's gentle, because He knows exactly how we're made. So when you fall short, talk to your Father, keep watching and praying, and remember that Jesus kept going when everyone else ran.
